signals.title: [doc] Record what blocks lifting the setuptools ceiling and replacing sphinxcontrib-redoc
signals.text: > **Stacked PR.** Fourth in a chain: #65456 (pin ReDoc) → #65457 (spec validity) → #65458 (declare 3.0.3) → this. It's independent in substance and touches only `doc/requirements-doc.txt`, so it can be retargeted to `master` if you'd rather take it on its own. ## Why this change is needed The `setuptools==80.9.0` pin in `doc/requirements-doc.txt` exists because `sphinxcontrib-redoc` imports `pkg_resources` at module load, and setuptools 82 removed it. The comment ends with "Lifting this ceiling means replacing or vendoring that extension," which leaves two questions open: 1. Is `sphinxcontrib-redoc` actually the *only* thing in the doc environment that needs `pkg_resources`? If not, removing it wouldn't lift the ceiling anyway. 2. Is there a usable replacement? I evaluated both. This records the answers so the next person hitting this pin doesn't re-derive them. ## Related changes Fourth in the chain above. No functional dependency on the three below it. ## What changes A comment in `doc/requirements-doc.txt`. No behavior change, no dependency change, no build change. ## Finding 1: `sphinxcontrib-redoc` is the sole blocker Installed every extension `conf.py` loads into an environment with no setuptools and no importable `pkg_resources`, then imported each one: | Result | Extensions | | --- | --- | | Import cleanly | `sphinx.ext.autodoc`, `viewcode`, `napoleon`, `doctest`, `coverage`, `autosummary`, `intersphinx`, `sphinx_click.ext`, `sphinxemoji`, `sphinx_copybutton`, `sphinx_sitemap`, `myst_nb`, `sphinxcontrib.autodoc_pydantic`, `sphinx_remove_toctrees`, `sphinx_design`, `sphinx_docsearch`, `sphinx_collections`, `sphinxext.opengraph` | | **Fails** | `sphinxcontrib.redoc` — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'` | That failure is the control: it reproduces the exact documented breakage, which confirms the test has power rather than passing vacuously. So dropping that one extension is sufficient to lift the ceiling. ## Finding 2: the maintained replacement works, in exactly one configuration `sphinxcontrib-openapi` 0.9.0 (released 2026-02-10, `requires_python >=3.10`) is the actively maintained alternative from the same `sphinx-contrib` org. It needs no setuptools, and it **does** render this spec with full request and response schemas and **zero warnings under `-W`** — but only with both of these: - `openapi_default_renderer = "httpdomain"` in `conf.py`, then a plain `.. openapi::` directive. - Operation `summary` fields as plain scalars rather than YAML block scalars. Neither is obvious, and each failure mode is silent or fatal rather than self-explaining: | Configuration | Schema content | Warnings under `-W` | | --- | --- | --- | | default renderer (`httpdomain:old`) | **none** — paths, parameters, status codes only | 0 | | `httpdomain:old` + `:request:` | request bodies only, as a raw JSON blob | 1 — [#171](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/171) | | `httpdomain:old` + `:examples:` | full | 1 — [#172](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/172) | | `httpdomain`, block-scalar summaries | full | 2 — [#173](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/173), plus literal `**` on the page | | **`httpdomain`, plain-scalar summaries** | **full** | **0** | The literal-asterisk defect is worth calling out because it's triggered by this repo's own spec: two operations use `summary: |`, which leaves a trailing newline in the value that the renderer interpolates straight into `**...**`. Changing those two lines to plain scalars is sufficient. The three configurations that genuinely don't work are filed upstream with minimal reproducers. ## So what actually gates migrating Not dependency hygiene, and not warnings. It's that ReDoc's standalone three-panel page would be replaced by output rendered inline in the site theme. That's a visible change to a published reference page, so it's a maintainer call rather than a docs-tooling cleanup, and this PR doesn't make it. Two things worth weighing whenever that call happens. In favor: the current page is a client-rendered JavaScript island. It's in no toctree, it's reachable only through a hardcoded `<api.html>` link at `rest.rst:94`, and its endpoint content isn't in the built HTML, so it doesn't participate in Sphinx search or cross-referencing. The trial build produced real Sphinx nodes and an `http-routingtable` index. Migrating would also let the `setuptools` ceiling lift, per finding 1. Against: it's a published reference page that readers may have bookmarked in its current form, and the inline rendering is a different reading experience rather than a strictly better one. My trial builds used the `basic` theme, so I can't show what it looks like under this site's actual theme without a full doc build. ## Checks - [x] Comment-only change; `pre-commit run` clean. - [x] Every claim in the comment verified by the trial builds described above.
signals.author: dstrodtman

signals.title: [doc] Render the Jobs API spec with sphinxcontrib-openapi instead of ReDoc
signals.text: > **Stacked PR.** Targets `doc-1513-declare-openapi-303` (#65458), which targets #65457. Review order is #65457 → #65458 → this. GitHub retargets automatically as each merges. > > **Conflicts with #65456 by design.** That PR pins `redoc_uri` to a specific ReDoc version; this one deletes `redoc_uri` entirely. If #65456 lands first I'll resolve the conflict here. If this lands, #65456 becomes moot and should be closed. Either order works — #65456 is worth keeping as the safe fix in case this one stalls in review. ## Why this change is needed `sphinxcontrib-redoc` is unmaintained. 1.6.0 is the latest release and dates from 2020; the `2.0.0a1` alpha still imports `pkg_resources`. Keeping it costs this repo three things: | Cost | Location | | --- | --- | | A `setuptools<82` ceiling, because the extension imports `pkg_resources` at module load and setuptools 82 removed it | `doc/requirements-doc.txt` | | A `misc.copy_overwrite` entry in `suppress_warnings`, because the extension redundantly copies its own bundled asset | `doc/source/conf.py` | | The renderer fetched from a third-party CDN at page-view time | `doc/source/conf.py` | All of that buys exactly one page. The Jobs API spec is the only consumer: `conf.py` had one `redoc` entry and there's no other OpenAPI document in the repo. There's a second, larger reason. **The current page is a client-rendered JavaScript island.** ReDoc has no source file at all — the extension synthesizes `api.html` from `conf.py`. So today the page: - is in **no toctree**, and - is reachable only through a hardcoded `` `... <api.html>`_ `` link at `rest.rst:94`, and - has **none of its endpoint content in the built HTML**, so it can't participate in Sphinx search or cross-referencing. ## Related changes Fourth in the chain above. Supersedes the "record why we stay on ReDoc" PR (#65459), which I'll close — its conclusion is obsolete now that this works. ## What changes - Swap `sphinxcontrib.redoc` → `sphinxcontrib.openapi` (0.9.0) in `conf.py` and `doc/requirements-doc.txt`, and regenerate the deplock. - Add a real `api.md`, put it in the `job-submission` toctree, and replace the raw `<api.html>` link with a `:ref:`. - Drop the now-unneeded `misc.copy_overwrite` suppression. - Change two operation `summary` fields from YAML block scalars to plain scalars (see below). - Update the `setuptools` comment: the `<82` ceiling's cause is gone. The pin itself is left in place, since unpinning is a separate resolve worth verifying on its own. `sphinxcontrib-openapi` is pure Python, from the same `sphinx-contrib` org, and needs no `pkg_resources`. The deplock diff is `-sphinxcontrib-redoc` and `+sphinxcontrib-openapi` plus its five dependencies (`sphinxcontrib-httpdomain`, `sphinx-mdinclude`, `deepmerge`, `mistune`, `picobox`). ## Verification Built with `make -C doc rtd-build`, which runs the RtD-faithful clean build with `-W`, matching `fail_on_warning: true`: ``` build succeeded. ``` Exit 0, and **zero `WARNING:`/`ERROR:` lines in the whole log**. `raydepsets --check` on `docbuild_depset_311` reports "Lock files are up to date." Checked against the built `api.html` rather than inferred: | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Request/response schemas rendered | Yes — `Request JSON Object` and `Response JSON Object` field lists, with `entrypoint`, `runtime_env`, `metadata`, and the rest, including types and required flags | | `$ref` and `allOf` resolution | Resolved, including through `JobDetails` | | Literal `**` on the page | None — zero docutils `problematic` nodes | | `http-routingtable` index | Generated | | Page in the sidebar, with prev/next pagination | Yes | | MyST page equivalent to the `.rst` draft it replaced | Yes — 8 httpdomain operation objects, identical `Parameters` / `Request JSON Object` / `Response JSON Object` / `Status Codes` field lists, no leaked rST, and both `:ref:` directions resolving with the right link text | ## Three non-obvious configuration details All three are commented at their sites in the diff, because all three fail quietly. **The renderer is selected via `openapi_default_renderer`, not by the directive spelling.** Writing `.. openapi:httpdomain::` in the page adds an `unknown directive name` warning, which is fatal under `fail_on_warning`. Selecting it in `conf.py` and using a plain `.. openapi::` avoids that. **The default renderer emits no request or response schemas at all** — just paths, parameters, and status codes. So leaving `openapi_default_renderer` unset would silently drop most of the reference content while still building green. That's the trap worth knowing about if anyone touches this later. **The `openapi` directive can't be a bare MyST fence; it has to be wrapped in `eval-rst`.** `sphinxcontrib-openapi` emits reStructuredText into a `ViewList` and hands it to `nested_parse`, but MyST's `nested_parse` renders that content as Markdown. A ```` ```{openapi} ```` fence therefore builds green with zero warnings while silently degrading the entire page: every `.. http:get::` and `:resjson:` line renders as literal text, so nothing becomes an httpdomain object and the page has no field lists, no anchors, and no search or cross-referencing. That's a worse failure than the one above, and just as quiet. ## Why the summary fields change `sphinxcontrib-openapi`'s renderer interpolates an operation's `summary` into `**...**` without stripping it. A YAML block scalar (`summary: |`) leaves a trailing newline in the value, so the markup opens on one line and closes on the next, docutils can't pair it, and readers see literal asterisks. Filed upstream as [sphinx-contrib/openapi#173](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/173). Two operations used block scalars (`GET /api/version` and `POST /api/jobs`); the other six already used plain scalars. Converting those two is the whole fix and changes no rendered text. ## What this gives up, honestly **Request and response samples.** ReDoc rendered example payloads; this doesn't. It isn't a configuration choice — both routes to examples are blocked by upstream bugs, and I've confirmed each against this spec: - `:generate-examples-from-schemas:` crashes with `ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required` ([#166](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/166)). Example generation can't handle an `allOf` that targets a non-object schema, which is exactly how `JobDetails` attaches descriptions to the `JobType` and `JobStatus` string enums. - `:response-examples-for:` is rejected as an unknown option ([#165](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/165)). `api.md` carries a comment recording this so nobody re-derives it, and I've added the reproduction detail to both upstream issues. Weighed against gaining search, cross-referencing, navigation, a dependency that's actually maintained, and no third-party CDN at page-view time, losing sample payloads seemed like the right trade — but it is a real loss, and it's reasonable to want the upstream fixes first instead. I've also filed [#171](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/171), [#172](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/172), and [#173](https://github.com/sphinx-contrib/openapi/issues/173), each with a minimal reproducer, and am planning PRs for them. ## Checks - [x] `make -C doc rtd-build`: build succeeded, zero warnings. - [x] `raydepsets --check`: lock files up to date. - [x] Built page inspected for schema content, `allOf`/`$ref` resolution, and stray markup. - [x] `pre-commit run` clean. - [ ] Read the Docs preview reviewed for the appearance change.

signals.title: [doc] llms.txt: tell agents the page links also serve Markdown
signals.text: ## Summary Follow-up to #64458. Adds one line to `llms.txt` telling agents that the page links also serve Markdown. Read the Docs serves a Markdown rendering of any page **from that page's own `.html` URL**, under an `Accept: text/markdown` request. There is no separate `.md` file to link to — `page.md`, `page.html.md`, `/md/<page>.md`, and `?format=md` all 404, and no `Link: rel=alternate` header advertises one. So the `.html` links `llms.txt` already emits *are* the Markdown links. Nothing in the file says so, and an agent has no way to discover it. ``` # Ray > Ray is an open-source unified compute framework for scaling AI and Python workloads… Full page text, grouped by section, is in [llms-full.txt](https://docs.ray.io/en/master/llms-full.txt). Request the links that follow with the HTTP header `Accept: text/markdown` to retrieve a Markdown rendering of the page. ## Overview … ``` ## The header has to be explicit Measured against `docs.ray.io/en/master/data/data.html`: | `Accept:` sent | returns | |---|---| | `*/*` — the default for curl, `requests`, `httpx` | `text/html` | | `text/html,application/xhtml+xml,*/*;q=0.8` — browser default | `text/html` | | `text/plain` | `text/html` | | `text/markdown` | **`text/markdown`** | | `text/markdown, */*` | **`text/markdown`** | | `text/markdown;q=1.0, text/html;q=0.9` | **`text/markdown`** | A wildcard isn't enough; the type has to be named. A client gets Markdown only by asking deliberately, so the pointer has a real audience. ## Config-gated New `llms_txt_markdown_hint`, **default `False`**. Content negotiation is a property of the host, not of the generator — a build served from somewhere that doesn't negotiate Markdown would otherwise advertise a representation that doesn't exist. `conf.py` sets it `True` for Ray. ## Wording note It says "a Markdown rendering of **the page**", deliberately not "the source". What comes back is the built page converted to Markdown — front matter, then site chrome (`Skip to main content`, theme switcher, version picker), then the content. That is not what `_sources/<page>.<ext>.txt` returns, and `_sources` genuinely exists, so calling it "the source" would point agents at the wrong artifact. ## Why not link `_sources/<page>.<ext>.txt` instead Considered and rejected: - **It leaks the source format to the consumer.** master is **363 `.rst` to 232 `.md`**, so most pages would hand back reStructuredText, not Markdown — noisier for an agent than the HTML→Markdown conversion. - **The URL isn't derivable from the page URL** — it depends on each page's source suffix (`index.md.txt` vs `installation.rst.txt`). - **It isn't human-clickable.** - **It would churn.** As pages migrate to MyST, each link would change from `.rst.txt` to `.md.txt`. Negotiation happens on the rendered HTML, so it's identical for both source formats and survives the migration. - **It's redundant** — the verbatim source is already in the `llms-full.txt` shards. ## Testing ``` $ python doc/source/_ext/test_llms_txt.py PASS: llms_txt extension produced a correct index, Optional section, llms-full shards, excludes notebooks by source type, gates the Markdown pointer, and honors the llms_txt_build gate. $ ruff check doc/source/_ext/llms_txt.py doc/source/_ext/test_llms_txt.py All checks passed! ``` New `test_markdown_hint` covers both directions: the pointer appears in the header (asserted to sit before the first `##` section) when the config is on, and is absent when it's off. The header table above was produced by probing the live `docs.ray.io`. All three changed files route to `@ doc doc_api` under the current `.buildkite/test.rules.txt`, so `doc: test llms.txt extension` runs on this PR. Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open` finds no other open PR touching `llms.txt` or Markdown content negotiation. ## AI assistance Drafted with Claude Code. The behavioural claims here (which `Accept` values return what, which `.md` URL forms 404, the negotiated output including page chrome) were each verified against the live site rather than assumed.
signals.author: ronny-anyscale

signals.title: [docs] Sync the vendored KubeRay CRD API reference
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Vendors the generated KubeRay CRD API reference at `doc/source/cluster/kubernetes/references/api.md` from `ray-project/kuberay` release tag v1.6.2, pinned at commit [`0a9eabd`](https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay/blob/0a9eabde561ab59ab4bbe626072c359da9214484/docs/reference/api.md). Opened automatically. The upstream file is a build artifact that `elastic/crd-ref-docs` generates from the Go CRD types in `ray-operator/apis/ray/`, and KubeRay's `ray-operator-verify-api-docs` CI job fails on drift between the two, so the content is verified upstream before it reaches here. That job covers `release-*` branches as well as `master`, so a release tag's artifact carries the same guarantee. This syncs from the latest KubeRay *release*, not from `master`. Master carries CRD surface that no release ships, and documenting it here would advertise fields a reader can't use. The `ray.io/v1alpha1` section is stripped on the way in. That API version is deprecated and on a removal runway (ray-project/kuberay#5124), and its cross-links collide with the v1 anchors (ray-project/kuberay#5091). With one package left, the `Packages` index and the `ray.io/v1` heading restate the page's own subject, so both are dropped and the headings under them move up to h2. Sphinx's right-hand page nav lists h2 only, so this is what puts the CRD types in it. Heading text is untouched, so the anchors cross-links resolve against don't move. A page intro replaces the generated package blurb those headings carried, naming the resource types read off the page's own index. ## Checks Content-only: the single changed file is documentation under `doc/`, so the `docs-go` scope guard applies cleanly. The Read the Docs preview build on this PR is the gate — a green build means the regenerated reference still renders and all of its in-page anchors resolve. Nothing else in this PR. If it contains any other change, something is wrong with the sync job.

signals.title: [serve] Deflake test_gcs_failure router tests
signals.text: test_new_router_on_gcs_failure sends a fixed 10 requests to 2 replicas and asserts it saw exactly 2 distinct pids. Routing between two idle replicas is a fair coin flip per request, PowerOfTwoChoicesRequestRouter.choose_replicas randomizes the pair order and _select_from_candidate_replicas breaks ties with a strict `<`, so a fixed count has a 2*(1/2)^10 chance of never hitting one of them. Cutting the loop to 3 requests to accelerate it (predicted 25%) failed 5 of 28 executions with a single-pid set; the same run with this change failed 0 of 28. Replace the three fixed-count loops with one helper that keeps the 10-request baseline batch and then tops up until every replica has served one. Every request must still succeed, so the "requests work while GCS is down" property is intact. Also give the six wait_for_condition calls that were inheriting the 10s default an explicit 30s -- they wait on replica startup and router propagation, which take tens of seconds on a loaded CI box -- and unify the per-request deadlines, the tightest of which was 1s.

signals.title: Bump mlflow from 3.11.1 to 3.13.0rc0 in /python
signals.text:
Bumps [mlflow](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow) from 3.11.1 to 3.13.0rc0.
Release notes

Sourced from mlflow's releases.

v3.13.0rc0

We're excited to announce MLflow 3.13.0rc0, which deepens agent observability, tightens permissions, and broadens deployment options:

Major New Features:

  • RBAC + Admin UI: Major overhaul of MLflow's Role-Based Access Control — legacy per-resource permission tables collapsed into role_permissions, unified per-user permission APIs under /mlflow/users/permissions/*, workspace USE permission lets users create experiments and registered models, default roles are seeded on workspace creation, prompt is promoted to a first-class RBAC resource_type, and a new 4-page Admin UI (account widget, /account page, Platform Admin pages, backend auth endpoints) opens to workspace managers scoped per their workspace. (#22855, #22857, #22859, #22928, #22929, #22941, #22973, #23086, #23247, #23248, #23337, #23379, @​PattaraS)

  • Coding-Agent Tracing as Plugins: Claude Code, OpenClaw, Ollama, and OpenAI Codex are now wired into the AI Gateway as first-class assistant providers, plus a Claude Code TypeScript plugin with a setup wizard and settings.local.json support. The legacy Python autolog hook for mlflow autolog claude is replaced by the new official plugin, and a coding-agent endpoint creation flow is now available directly in the AI Gateway UI. (#20414, #22098, #22566, #22717, #23218, #23285, #23339, #23430, #23517, @​B-Step62, @​joelrobin18, @​Gkrumbach07, @​SuperSonnix71, @​TomeHirata)

  • Trace Archival: End-to-end trace archival across the tracking stack. Includes archival configuration models, OTLP and artifact helpers, SQLAlchemy archival passes, archive-aware retrieval fallback, plus workspace/experiment/server-level archival settings in the UI. Read archived traces back seamlessly. (#23359, @​mprahl)

  • Helm Charts for Kubernetes Deployment: First-class Helm chart for deploying MLflow to Kubernetes clusters — production-ready configuration, ingress, persistence, and appVersion wired to the released MLflow image. Get from helm install to a running tracking server without writing your own manifests. (#21973, @​WeichenXu123)

  • mlflow.genai.test_agent for Automated Agent Stress-Testing: New API for stress-testing GenAI agents — generate adversarial inputs, replay them through your agent, and review the resulting traces in MLflow. Wires into the existing evaluation flow and assessment APIs. (#22990, @​serena-ruan)

  • OpenTelemetry Span Links: Tracing now supports the OpenTelemetry Link entity via LiveSpan.add_link(), letting you connect causally related spans across traces. (#22797, @​khaledsulayman)

  • Database Replica Routing: The SQL tracking store now supports reader/writer instance routing for database replicas, so read-heavy MLflow deployments can scale horizontally without overloading the primary. (#22910, @​ravidarbha)

Stay tuned for the full release, which will include even more features and bug fixes.

To try out this release candidate, please run:

pip install mlflow==3.13.0rc0

v3.12.0

MLflow 3.12.0 includes several major features and improvements

Major New Features

  • 🖼️ Multimodal Tracing: Users can now store multimodal content in tracing spans as artifact attachments instead of inline binary data. We've also patched the UI to support the new mlflow-attachment:// style URI, with rich rendering available for PDFs, audio, and images.
  • 🤖 Codex, Gemini, Qwen coding agent tracing support: Similar to our Claude Code tracing integration, we've now added support for the Codex, Gemini, and Qwen coding agent platforms as well!
  • 🛡️ Gateway guardrails: You can now set guardrails on your gateway endpoints to prevent unsafe or non-compliant model inputs and outputs. Try it out in the MLflow UI!
  • ⚡ Trace table pagination: The traces tab is now paginated, rather than fetching all traces up to a limit of 1000. This improves initial load time, and makes the page feel more responsive overall.

Breaking Changes

  • [Scoring] Deprecate enable_mlserver in pyfunc serving backend (#22994, @​B-Step62)

Other Assorted Features & Improvements:

  • [UI] Add coding agents section to AI Gateway quick start (#23006, @​TomeHirata)
  • [Tracing] feat: record caller in gateway traces from request headers (#22926, @​TomeHirata)
  • [] Run guardrails on passthrough endpoints; skip response_format for non-chat payloads (#22856, @​TomeHirata)
  • [] Gateway: preserve client auth header for subscription-based CLI tools (claude-cli, Codex-Desktop, GeminiCLI) (#22915, @​TomeHirata)
  • [Tracing] Expose Codex and Qwen Code hooks as installable CLI binaries (#22853, @​kriscon-db)
  • [Tracking / UI] Add Portkey as a supported AI Gateway provider (#22830, @​sairavuri-sudo)
  • [Tracking] Cache successful basic-auth credential checks to eliminate per-request PBKDF2 (#22817, @​PattaraS)
  • [] Add last_updated_at field to model catalog entries (#22838, @​copilot-swe-agent)
  • [Evaluation] Enable third-party scorer registration in OSS MLflow (#22634, @​smoorjani)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from mlflow's changelog.

CHANGELOG

3.15.1 (2026-08-03)

MLflow 3.15.1 is a patch release that includes bug fixes and documentation updates.

Bug fixes:

  • [Model Registry] Skip env_pack on ARM client images (#24762) (#24835, @​qyc)
  • [Scoring / Tracking] Harden version parsing against missing/non-PEP440 versions on Databricks Serverless (+ lint rule) (#24799) (#24813, @​PattaraS)

Documentation updates:

  • [Docs] Clarify scorer versioning documentation (#24769) (#24805, @​nihalmenon)

3.15.0 (2026-07-31)

MLflow 3.15.0 includes several major features and improvements

Major New Features

  • 🧩 MCP Registry: A centralized catalog for registering, versioning, and sharing Model Context Protocol servers — with semantic-versioned configs, promotable aliases, tags, auto-discovered tools, and ready-made connection instructions for Claude Code and .mcp.json. Manage it from the UI, REST API, or Python!
  • 🤖 MLflow Assistant enhancements: The in-app AI assistant now supports multiple LLM providers (Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible/Gateway endpoints) chosen from a single settings page, displays live per-session token usage and estimated cost in the composer, and is easier to set up — mlflow agent setup can enable it in one prompt, with API keys stored securely in the Gateway's LLM Connections.
  • 🗂️ Sharable table views: Save named views of the Runs table — capturing columns, order, widths, filters, and sort — and share them by URL.
  • ⚡ Proxy-less artifact upload/download via presigned URLs: Large artifact transfers can now bypass the tracking server and talk directly to cloud storage (e.g. S3) through presigned URLs, cutting server load and timeouts on big files. We fall back to proxied transfer automatically for backward compatibility.
  • 🖼️ Multi-modal attachments in LLM judges: {{ trace }} judges created with make_judge() can now see images captured in trace spans via a new get_span_image tool, which fetches attachments as base64 data URLs and passes them to multimodal models (Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible via litellm) — enabling evaluation of vision tasks, screenshots, and other visual content.

signals.title: [docs] Convert the nine highest-traffic landing pages from RST to MyST
signals.text:
## Why are these changes needed? MyST Markdown is the standard for Ray doc pages, and a lint check already rejects newly-added `.rst`. This is the first batch of the conversion of the existing hand-written prose under `doc/source/`. The batch is the nine highest-traffic, lowest-risk pages in the tree: short prose intros plus a `toctree`, no tabs, no doctests, no includes. 679 lines total, and 23% of all `.rst` page views over the last 90 days. Starting here validates the conversion end to end on the pages where any regression is immediately obvious, at close to zero conversion risk. | File | Lines | | --- | --- | | `index.rst` | 27 | | `ray-overview/examples.rst` | 10 | | `ray-overview/use-cases.rst` | 187 | | `data/api/api.rst` | 22 | | `train/api/api.rst` | 256 | | `ray-core/key-concepts.rst` | 50 | | `cluster/key-concepts.rst` | 90 | | `ray-core/api/index.rst` | 15 | | `ray-overview/examples/index.rst` | 22 | The conversion is format-only. Every label name, `toctree` entry, directive, and prose line is preserved, so the rendered HTML should be unchanged and the preview-versus-`/en/master` diff should be empty. No URLs change: Sphinx maps `foo.rst` and `foo.md` to the same `foo.html`. ### Conversions worth a second look - **`index.rst` has no heading**, so its browser title comes entirely from `.. title:: Welcome to Ray!`. There's no MyST frontmatter equivalent, so it stays as RST in an `{eval-rst}` block. The file-level `:html_theme.sidebar_secondary.remove:` field becomes frontmatter, matching `404.md`. - **`train/api/api.rst` keeps its 19 `autosummary` directives and its `.. currentmodule::` as column-0 RST inside `{eval-rst}` blocks** — the pattern `serve/api/index.md` already uses. The two labels that sit directly above an `autosummary` stay inside the block so their targets still register. - **`ray-core/key-concepts.rst` has a two-item list that docutils folds into the preceding paragraph**, because no blank line separates them. [The rendered page](https://docs.ray.io/en/master/ray-core/key-concepts.html#environment-dependencies) shows it as one `

`. CommonMark *would* turn it into a real `

    `, so the leading `1.` and `2.` are escaped to keep the current rendering. Happy to unescape and let it become a real list if that's preferred, but that's a rendering change rather than a conversion. - **`use-cases.rst` keeps the `.. raw:: html` body of its two `query-param-ref` blocks as RST.** That directive parses its own content with a `docutils` parser at `doctree-resolved` time, independent of the host file's format, so the content has to stay RST either way. ## The CI change in the second commit Converting `data/api/api.rst` and `ray-core/api/index.rst` surfaced a real gap in `ci/ray_ci/doc/autodoc.py`, which is why this PR isn't docs-only. The API-discrepancy check builds each team's documented-API set by walking its landing page's `toctree`. The walker only recognized the RST directive form (`.. toctree::` followed by indented entries). A MyST `toctree` is a directive fence with entries at column 0, so the walker's "first unindented line ends the block" heuristic stops on the very first entry. The `data` and `core` teams would have walked no children at all, collapsing their documented set to the landing page itself and flagging every child page's `autosummary` entries as undocumented public APIs. `serve/api/index.md` was already Markdown, but it declares its whole surface inline with no page-level `toctree`, so this path had never been exercised. The second commit teaches the walker the fence form alongside the RST form, points the `data`, `core`, and `train` `head_doc_file` entries at the converted pages, and adds a regression test. The `toctree` entries themselves are unchanged, so the walk reaches exactly the same set of child files as before. The `.buildkite` rules fixtures and the two notebook links that named a converted file by path are refreshed in the same commit. The rules themselves match on directory prefix and on both extensions, so what each path emits is unchanged. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open --search "MyST"` and a search for the converted paths return no other open PR touching these files or this conversion. #65469 is the companion skill change and is deliberately separate, so a rule change isn't buried in a content PR. AI assistance was used to prepare this change. ## Related issue number Part of the ongoing RST-to-MyST conversion of `doc/source/`. Subsequent batches follow the same traffic-weighted ordering. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - [x] Unit tests: `ci/ray_ci/doc/test_autodoc.py` gains coverage for the MyST fence form; the walk over the three converted API landing pages was verified to reach the same child set as before. - [x] Release tests: not applicable. - [x] This PR is not tested (please justify below): the decisive check for the conversion itself is the Read the Docs preview build under `fail_on_warning: true`, plus a rendered diff against `/en/master`. Please hold the merge until both are confirmed clean.

signals.title: [docs] Lowercase "Ray dashboard" across the docs
signals.text: ## Why this change "Dashboard" is a generic noun, so it stays lowercase next to a product name for the same reason "autoscaler" does. That's the convention #65239 settles, on @win5923's reasoning in [this review comment](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/65239#issuecomment-5283520022). This PR applies it across the docs. Splitting it out from the rule change keeps each one reviewable on its own: #65239 is the rule and the tooling, this is the mechanical sweep, and the diff here is casing with no prose rewrites. Same split as #65423, which retires "Ray Pod." **This depends on #65239 landing first.** If the convention changes in that review, this sweep changes with it. ## Scope All of `doc/source`, `.md` and `.rst`. 215 replacements across 53 pages, in prose: body text, headings, front matter and `.. meta::` descriptions, a glossary term, table cells, image alt text, and link and cross-reference text. Three commits, each reviewable on its own: the Kubernetes pages, the same term across the rest of the docs, and then the bare "Dashboard" that the first two left behind. The first commit covers `cluster/kubernetes/`, which is where #65239 scopes its Vale ruleset. The second extends the same convention to the rest, so it holds on every surface rather than only where the tooling happens to point: `ray-observability/`, `serve/`, `ray-core/`, `train/`, `ray-security/`, `ray-overview/`, the non-Kubernetes `cluster/` pages, `data/`, `rllib/`, and `ray-references/`. Headings are included deliberately. This guide requires sentence case for every heading, so "## Step 5: Access the Ray Dashboard" was already a defect on two counts. **The `ray-observability/getting-started` page title changes**, from "Ray Dashboard" to "Ray dashboard." That's the canonical dashboard page, so it's the most visible line in the diff and worth a deliberate look. Cross-references to it that don't set their own text pick the new title up automatically. ## Applied by script, reviewed by hand The sweep ran from a fence-aware script rather than find-and-replace, because a blind pass would have hit literal blocks and rewritten CLI output. It tracks Markdown code fences, treats MyST directive fences such as ```` ```{admonition} ```` as the prose they contain, and tracks rST literal blocks introduced by both `.. code-block::` and a trailing `::`. I reviewed all 162 replacements and each of the 9 exclusions individually. ## Deliberately not changed **Nine uses inside literal blocks**, because the rule governs prose. Eight are shell comments, five of them `# Step 7: Check Ray Dashboard...` in `k8s-ecosystem/ingress.md`. The ninth is literal CLI output in `user-guides/kubectl-plugin.md` (`Ray Dashboard: http://localhost:8265`), where changing it would misreport what the command prints. That leaves a page or two with a lowercase heading above a capitalized shell comment. I'd rather flag that than quietly edit code blocks in a prose sweep. Happy to include the eight comments if a reviewer prefers consistency within the page. **One use in `cluster/kubernetes/configs/static-ray-cluster.tls.yaml`**, a comment in a sample manifest rather than a docs page. **Nothing, as it turns out.** An earlier revision of this description claimed 217 bare capitalized "Dashboard" uses were being left alone. That number was wrong: the command behind it piped `grep -o` output into a `grep -v` filter that could never match, so it counted every occurrence of the word including the ones inside "Ray Dashboard". The real figure was 93, and the third commit sweeps the 54 of those that are the generic noun. What stays capitalized is listed above. **`README.rst` and the `python/` docstrings.** Eight files outside `doc/` use the term, mostly in docstrings that render into the API reference. Different surface, different owners. ## Bare "Dashboard" The third commit covers the 54 uses of a bare capitalized "Dashboard" that the term sweep left behind, which otherwise put "the Dashboard" next to "the Ray dashboard" on the same page. Most are a pure case change. Fifteen needed an article, because the prose used the word as a bare proper noun: "expose Dashboard outside the Cluster" becomes "expose the dashboard outside the Cluster", and three sentences opening "Dashboard is..." become "The dashboard is...". The installation extras table is the one place where a bare lowercase "dashboard" would have read badly, sitting in a list of Ray library names ("Core, Dashboard, Cluster Launcher"). Those rows and the tip below them now say "Ray dashboard". Left capitalized, because these aren't the generic noun: - CloudWatch's Agent, Dashboard, and Alarm config files, plus Grafana's Dashboard and Default Dashboard. - The literal **Open Dashboard** button label in the History Server UI. - Title and label positions where any word would capitalize: the "Dashboard (Web UI)" section title, a `Dashboard` tab label, and a `**Dashboard**` list label. - Twelve uses inside literal blocks, one of which is dashboard log output. ## Six adjacent lines Lowercasing one word of an otherwise title-case heading reads as a botched edit, so where that happened the whole heading goes sentence case: - `cluster/configure-manage-dashboard.md`: "Configuring and Managing Ray Dashboard" to "Configuring and managing Ray dashboard," plus the two link texts and one `:ref:` text that mirror that page title. - `ray-observability/user-guides/profiling.md`: "Ray Dashboard View" to "Ray dashboard view." - `ray-core/internals/token-authentication.rst`: "Ray Dashboard Flow" to "Ray dashboard flow." One more of the same kind in the first commit: alt text in `user-guides/kuberay-dashboard.md` read "KubeRay dashboard List of RayJobs" after the swap, so "List" lowercases too. ## Known cosmetic wart `user-guides/kuberay-history-server.md:13` now reads "see [Ray dashboard](https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-observability/getting-started.html)" against a target whose published title is still title case. This PR retitles that page, so the two converge once it lands. The sentence is redundant as written either way. ## Testing No code, no API, no behavior change. Most replacements are identical in length. The ones that aren't are the fifteen that gained an article and the installation table rows, so rST title underlines needed checking rather than assuming: one title, "Set up Dashboard" becoming "Set up the dashboard", grew past its underline and is fixed. Verified against `master` that the change introduces no other short underline anywhere in `doc/source`. Verified with Vale 3.12.0, running the ruleset from #65239 against this branch: the `Ray Dashboard` and `KubeRay Dashboard` swaps go from 44 alerts to **0** on the paths that ruleset scopes, and `doc/source/data/` holds at 170 with no new alerts. Vale doesn't cover the other paths in this PR, and it has no rule for the bare noun at all, so the rest was verified by hand against a categorized list of every occurrence. Verified by hand that nothing in the repo references any of the changed heading strings, so no cross-reference or link text goes stale. Nothing here is enforced in CI. The Vale pre-commit hook remains scoped to `doc/source/data/`. ## AI assistance Written with AI assistance (Claude). The script is mine, I've reviewed every replacement and exclusion individually, and I can defend the change end to end.

signals.title: [doc] rst-to-myst: add a render-diff check and fix three mapping errors
signals.text:
## Why are these changes needed? The `rst-to-myst` skill treated a green `fail_on_warning` build as near-sufficient evidence that a conversion was faithful. It isn't, and #65467 proved it: converting the first batch of landing pages produced three regressions that built clean and emitted no warning anywhere. - **`doc/source/index.rst` carries its browser title in a `.. title::` directive.** That directive does not set the document title from inside an `{eval-rst}` block, so the site root rendered as ``. - **An RST `.. image::` with no `:alt:`** takes its alt text from the URI and emits a bare ``. The skill mapped it to `![](URL)`, which emits `alt=""` wrapped in a `

`. - **`default_role = "code"`** makes a single-backtick RST literal render as ``. The skill called the Markdown single-backtick "byte-faithful"; it drops the `code` class. None of the three is visible to a static source check, and none of them fails a build. The campaign has 345 files left to convert, so the fix has to be a check rather than a caution. ## What changed **`render_diff.py`** — fetches the RtD PR preview and `/en/master` for each page, extracts `

`, normalizes the host, release string, and search-highlight params, and diffs. ```bash python3 doc/.claude/skills/rst-to-myst/render_diff.py \ https://anyscale-ray--65467.com.readthedocs.build/en/65467/ \ index.html cluster/key-concepts.html ray-overview/use-cases.html ``` It filters the two differences every MyST page shows against an RST page, both verified inert: - `class="tex2jax_ignore mathjax_ignore"`, which myst-parser stamps on the root `
` of every MyST document. - The missing `code` class above. Grepping `pydata-sphinx-theme.css`, `theme.css`, and `doc/source/_static/css/` finds no rule for it, and every already-converted page in the tree renders without it. Plain backticks are the house choice; `--keep-benign` shows the difference if you want it. It also labels `ray-overview/examples.html`, which differs between *any* two builds because `custom_directives.py` picks its gallery icons with `random.randint`. **`SKILL.md`** — promotes the render diff from a one-line afterthought at the end of Verification to a required step, and says what it is for: steps 1–3 are all source-side or resolution-side, so step 4 is the only one that can catch this class. Corrects the `.. image::` mapping row, adds rows for `.. figure::` and `.. title::`, adds Hard rule 5 covering all three page-identity constructs, and rewrites the `default_role` construct note. The guidance is deliberately "read the diffs," not "expect zero." Byte-identical is not always the right bar — a caption-less `{figure}` or a deliberate alt-text addition shows up here too — so the question the script answers is whether every diff is explainable. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open --search "rst-to-myst"` returns no open PR touching this skill or `doc/.claude/skills/`. #65467 is the content batch that motivated this; it deliberately does not carry the skill change, since a rule change buried in a content PR ships unreviewed. ## Related issue number Follow-up to #65467. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - **Commands run and results.** `python3 render_diff.py --help` parses. Run against #65467's preview across all nine converted pages, it reports `index.html`, `cluster/key-concepts.html`, and `ray-overview/use-cases.html` as `IDENTICAL` after the fixes and correctly flags `ray-overview/examples.html` as known-nondeterministic. Run against the same preview *before* those fixes, it surfaced all three regressions above, which is how they were found. Benign-class filtering verified in both directions with and without `--keep-benign`. - Release tests: not applicable. - This PR touches `doc/.claude/` only, which no Bazel target or `.buildkite` rule references, so it pulls no CI suite. AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

signals.title: [docs] Convert the seven card-grid library front doors from RST to MyST
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? MyST Markdown is the standard for Ray doc pages, and a lint check already rejects newly-added `.rst`. This is the second batch of the conversion of the existing hand-written prose under `doc/source/`, following #65467. The batch is the seven library front-door pages. They share one pattern: a `grid` of `grid-item-card`s, some `tab-set`s, `literalinclude` pulls, and a `toctree`. 1,889 lines, and 18% of all `.rst` page views over the last 90 days. | File | Lines | Constructs | | --- | --- | --- | | `tune/index.rst` | 299 | 3 tabs, 6 cards, 3 literalinclude, `callout`/`annotations` | | `ray-core/walkthrough.rst` | 132 | 3 cards, 4 literalinclude | | `data/data.rst` | 187 | 5 cards, 1 testcode | | `train/train.rst` | 233 | 10 cards, nested `div`, `raw:: html :file:` | | `ray-overview/installation.rst` | 548 | 2 tab-sets, 3 tables, 20 named link targets | | `ray-overview/ray-libraries.rst` | 378 | 17 cards | | `cluster/getting-started.rst` | 112 | 4 cards | The conversion is format-only. Every label name, `toctree` entry, directive, and prose line is preserved, so the rendered HTML should be unchanged. No URLs change: Sphinx maps `foo.rst` and `foo.md` to the same `foo.html`. Unlike #65467, this batch needs no CI or `BUILD.bazel` changes. None of the seven files is named in `doc/BUILD.bazel`, in a `.buildkite` rules fixture, or in `ci/ray_ci/doc`. `data/data.rst`'s one real `testcode`/`testoutput` pair stays covered by the `data` doctest rule's `source/**/*.md` glob. ## Card grids convert to native MyST Every card grid already in a `.md` page (`cluster/vms/index.md`, `cluster/kubernetes/index.md`, `ray-overview/index.md`, `serve/index.md`) is wrapped in `{eval-rst}` and left as RST. This batch uses native MyST fences instead: ```markdown ::::{grid} 1 2 2 2 :gutter: 1 :::{grid-item-card} **Title** ^^^ Body text. +++ ```{button-ref} some-label :color: primary Button text ``` ::: :::: ``` sphinx-design supports MyST first-class — its own docs are MyST and it ships a `snippets/myst/` tree. The `^^^` and `+++` separators are matched by `REGEX_HEADER`/`REGEX_FOOTER` and split out of the raw content lines before anything parses them, so they're format-agnostic. `GridDirective` and `GridItemCardDirective` are ordinary docutils directives registered through `app.add_directive`, which MyST dispatches exactly the way it already dispatches `{tab-set}` in a dozen `.md` pages today. The one thing to know: these directives call `self.state.nested_parse`, so under MyST their content parses as **Markdown**. Any RST left inside a native card renders as literal text instead of erroring. That's why the nested `button-ref`/`button-link`/`image`/`figure` directives all convert too, and it's the specific thing the render diff below was run to confirm. A follow-up PR converts the four existing `{eval-rst}`-wrapped grids so the tree ends up with one pattern rather than two. ## Conversions worth a second look - **`installation.rst` keeps its RST simple table in `{eval-rst}`.** The nightly-wheel table for Linux is a `====`-delimited simple table whose cells are RST named-target references. Converting it to a Markdown or `{list-table}` table changes the rendered HTML, so it stays RST along with the eight target definitions it uses, which now live in the same block. The MacOS and Windows tabs were already `list-table`s, so those become `{list-table}` with the URLs inlined as Markdown links. - **`tune/index.rst` had two link forms that don't survive transcription.** `` `Ray Serve`_ `` pointed at `../serve/index.html`, a relative `.html` URL that renders in RST but is a cross-reference target under MyST; it becomes `` {doc}`Ray Serve </serve/index>` ``. Separately, `` `terminating bad runs early <tune-scheduler-hyperband>`_ `` is an RST *external* link to a bare label name, so today it renders as `<a href="tune-scheduler-hyperband">` — a dead relative URL. Sibling lines in the same paragraph use `:ref:` for the same targets, so it becomes `{ref}`. **That is a deliberate rendering change and the one place the diff below is not empty.** Happy to keep the dead link if you'd rather this PR stay strictly format-only. - **`tune/index.rst` is the only file in the tree using the `callout` and `annotations` directives** (`doc/source/_ext/callouts.py`). Both `nested_parse`, so their content is now Markdown; the `<1>`/`<2>` annotation markers are literal text under both parsers. - **`train/train.rst`'s logo block** nests `div` inside `div` around a `raw:: html` with a `:file:` option. It converts to nested colon fences with a `{raw}` fence inside. - **`ray-overview/getting-started.md` linked to `../tune/index.rst`**, which would dangle after the rename. It becomes a `{doc}` reference. ## Verification - Static checks pass on all seven files: frontmatter parses, backtick and colon fences balance at every width, all 14 labels preserved, no residual RST outside fences, no `.rst`/`.html#` link forms, `testcode`/`testoutput` counts match the originals. - Read the Docs preview under `fail_on_warning: true`. - `render_diff.py` against `/en/master` for all seven pages. **Please hold the merge until I've posted those results in a comment.** ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open` shows no other PR touching these seven files or this conversion, other than #65468, which changes six lines inside `installation.rst`'s extras table. Whichever lands first, the other rebases. ## Related issue number Part of the ongoing RST-to-MyST conversion of `doc/source/`, following #65467. Subsequent batches follow the same traffic-weighted ordering. AI assistance was used to prepare this change. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - [x] Unit tests: not applicable; no `BUILD.bazel` or CI wiring changes in this batch. - [x] Release tests: not applicable. - [x] This PR is not tested (please justify below): the decisive checks for a conversion are the RtD preview build under `fail_on_warning: true` and the rendered diff against `/en/master`, both listed above.

signals.title: [doc] rst-to-myst: add the sphinx-design card-grid mapping
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Stacked on #65469. Converting the seven card-grid front doors in #65470 exercised a part of the `rst-to-myst` skill that had no mapping at all: `grid`, `grid-item-card`, `grid-item`, `button-ref`, `button-link`, and `div`. The skill covered sphinx-design tabs and dropdowns but stopped short of cards, which are the dominant construct in batches 4 through 8. It also had no entry for RST named hyperlink targets (`` `text`_ `` plus a `.. _`text`: url` definition). `ray-overview/installation.rst` alone has twenty. ## What changed **Mapping rows** for the six sphinx-design directives above. **A construct note on card grids**, covering the two things that aren't obvious: - The `^^^` header and `+++` footer separators need no translation. sphinx-design matches them with `REGEX_HEADER`/`REGEX_FOOTER` in `cards.py` and splits them out of the raw content lines before anything parses them, so they're format-agnostic. - `GridDirective`, `GridItemCardDirective`, `div`, and Ray's own `callout`/`annotations` all call `self.state.nested_parse`, which under MyST parses their content as **Markdown**. RST left inside a native card doesn't warn — it renders as literal text through a green `fail_on_warning` build. Everything nested has to convert in the same pass, and the render diff is the only check that catches it. That second point also fixes a dangling reference: Verification step 4 already said the render diff is "the only step that catches Hard rule 5 or the `nested_parse` degradation below," and there was no such note below. Now there is. The note also records that four already-Markdown pages (`cluster/vms/index.md`, `cluster/kubernetes/index.md`, `ray-overview/index.md`, `serve/index.md`) wrap their grids in `{eval-rst}`, and says not to copy that into new conversions. A follow-up PR converts those four. **A construct note on named hyperlink targets** — inline them as Markdown links, except where an `{eval-rst}` table's cells reference them, in which case the definitions stay RST inside that same block so no target name is defined twice. **Two verified facts**, both checked against the pinned source rather than assumed: - `sphinx_design==0.7.0` supports MyST first-class. Its own docs are MyST, it ships a `snippets/myst/` tree, and its directives register through `app.add_directive`, so MyST's `{name}` dispatch reaches them like any other directive. - `_replace_numbers()` in `doc/source/_ext/callouts.py` discards its own result (`content.replace(...)` with no assignment), so the `<1>`-to-① substitution only happens in `CalloutIncludePostTransform`, over literal blocks. Annotation text keeps literal `<1>` markers under either parser. Flagging rather than fixing, since it's outside this PR's scope and the rendering is longstanding. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open --search "rst-to-myst"` returns #65469, which this is stacked on and which touches different sections of the same file. No other open PR touches `doc/.claude/skills/`. ## Related issue number Follow-up to #65469. Motivated by #65470, which deliberately doesn't carry this change, since a rule change buried in a content PR ships unreviewed. AI assistance was used to prepare this change. ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (`git commit -s`). - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` to lint the changes in this PR. - [x] I've included any doc changes needed for the change. - [x] Testing strategy - The claims about `^^^`/`+++` splitting, `nested_parse`, and directive registration were read off `sphinx_design==0.7.0`'s own source (`cards.py`, `grids.py`, `extension.py`), not inferred. The native-grid pattern the note prescribes is the one #65470 ships and render-diffs. - Release tests: not applicable. - This PR touches `doc/.claude/` only, which no Bazel target or `.buildkite` rule references, so it pulls no CI suite.

signals.title: [doc] Convert the four remaining wrapped card grids to native MyST
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? Stacked on #65470. Four pages are already Markdown but keep their sphinx-design card grids as RST inside an `{eval-rst}` block: | File | Cards | | --- | --- | | `cluster/kubernetes/index.md` | 6 | | `serve/index.md` | 5 | | `cluster/vms/index.md` | 4 | | `ray-overview/index.md` | 3 | That pattern predates native MyST card support and, until #65470, was the only card-grid precedent in the tree. Now that the seven highest-traffic front doors use native fences, these four are the remainder. Converting them leaves one pattern instead of two, so batches 4 through 8 have an unambiguous model to copy. ## What changed Each `{eval-rst}` grid becomes native colon fences, widest on the outside: ```markdown ::::{grid} 1 2 2 2 :gutter: 1 :class-container: container pb-3 :::{grid-item-card} :class-img-top: pt-2 w-75 d-block mx-auto fixed-height-img **Getting Started** ^^^ Body text. +++ ```{button-ref} some-label :color: primary :outline: :expand: Button text ``` ::: :::: ``` Format-only. Grid and card options, the `^^^` and `+++` separators, and every `button-ref` target are preserved verbatim. **The one non-mechanical part:** a native card's content parses as Markdown, not RST, so the `:doc:` and `:ref:` roles in the card bodies had to become `{doc}` and `{ref}` in the same pass. Left as RST they wouldn't warn — they'd render as literal text through a green build. `ray-overview/index.md` has six `:doc:` roles in one card and `serve/index.md` has ten `:ref:` roles across five, so this is the bulk of the non-whitespace diff. The separate `{eval-rst}` block in `cluster/kubernetes/index.md` holding an `.. image::` and a source-document comment is left alone. It isn't a grid, and folding it in would widen this PR past its stated scope. ## Verification - Fence balance checked at every colon width on all four files; backtick fences even; no residual `:doc:`/`:ref:`/``` `` ``` RST outside fences. - Read the Docs preview under `fail_on_warning: true`. - `render_diff.py` against `/en/master` for all four pages. **Please hold the merge until I've posted those results in a comment** — the render diff is the only check that catches a card whose nested content silently degraded. ## Not a duplicate `gh pr list --repo ray-project/ray --state open` shows no other PR touching these four files. ## Related issue number Follows #65470. signals.title: [Fix/n] Return External Consumer Bytes for Downstream Capacity to Activate Backpressure
signals.text: ## Description #64456 applies the block ref counter to track the object store memory and control backpressure signals based on downstream capacity, but this had lead to spilling in training pipelines. This is mainly due to backpressure not being applied to the terminal operator even though the external consumer is not consuming blocks quickly enough. This PR adds back the early return for `DownstreamCapacityBackpressurePolicy`'s `_get_downstream_capacity_size_bytes`, so that for terminal operators, the downstream capacity is the external consumer bytes tracked instead of 0. ## Related issues Fixes https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64456.

signals.title: [Core] Fix prepared bundle leak and scheduling stall when removing an in-flight placement group
signals.text: ## Description Removing a placement group while bundle preparation is still in flight can leak prepared raylet resources and leave the GCS placement-group scheduling gate stuck. The scheduler already documents that a `PrepareBundleResources` callback may never fire (e.g. when the target node dies), but cancellation and removal still waited on that callback: - `MarkScheduleCancelled` only recorded the cancelled state; already-prepared bundles were not released because cleanup waited for `OnAllBundlePrepareRequestReturned`, which requires *all* prepare callbacks to return. - A prepare reply arriving after cancellation was folded into the tracker but still waited for the remaining callbacks before any cleanup ran. - `RemovePlacementGroup` never released `scheduling_in_progress_id_`, so a later pending placement group was never scheduled. This change makes cancellation- and removal-time cleanup independent of the prepare callbacks that may never arrive: - `MarkScheduleCancelled` now destroys the already-prepared bundles immediately (skipped only while committing, where the commit path already handles cleanup). - A prepare reply that returns after cancellation releases the just-prepared bundle immediately instead of waiting for the remaining callbacks. - `RemovePlacementGroup` releases the scheduling token it owns, and the creation callbacks only release the token when the callback's placement group still owns it, so a stale callback from a removed group cannot clear a newer group's token. ## Related issues Fixes #64693 ## Additional information No API or wire-format changes. The regression tests model a prepare callback that never returns by withholding the reply on the mock raylet client, so they are deterministic. ## Tests - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_scheduler_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupSchedulerTest.PlacementGroupCancelledAfterPartialPrepareReleasesPreparedBundle --test_output=errors` — fails on master (no `RemovePlacementGroupBundles` RPC for the already-prepared bundle), passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_scheduler_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupSchedulerTest.PlacementGroupCancelledAfterLatePrepareSuccessReleasesNewBundle --test_output=errors` — fails on master, passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_manager_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupManagerTest.TestRemovingLeasingPlacementGroupUnblocksPending --test_output=errors` — fails on master (the pending placement group is never scheduled), passes with this change. - `bazel test //src/ray/gcs/tests:gcs_placement_group_manager_test --test_filter=GcsPlacementGroupManagerTest.TestLateCallbackDoesNotReleaseNextPlacementGroupToken --test_output=errors` — covers the scheduling-token guard: a late creation callback from a removed placement group must not release the token a newer group now owns. Fails on master, passes with this change. - The surrounding placement-group cancellation tests in both files (`DestroyCancelledPlacementGroup`, `PlacementGroupCancelledDuringCommit`, `PlacementGroupCancelledDuringPreparedPut`, `TestRemovingLeasingPlacementGroup`) pass.

signals.title: [Autoscaler][V2] Add ALLOCATION_GATED status for scaleGate fast fallback
signals.text: ## Why are these changes needed? When an external controller (e.g. Kueue) blocks a worker group from scaling up by setting `spec.workerGroupSpecs[i].scaleStrategy.scaleGate` (for example, on a quota-exceeded group), the autoscaler previously had no way to distinguish this "gated" condition from a genuine allocation failure. A requested instance for a gated group would sit in `REQUESTED`/`ALLOCATED` until the allocate-status timeout elapsed before the scheduler could fall back to a lower-priority group. This PR introduces a dedicated `ALLOCATION_GATED` instance status so gated launches fail fast and the scheduler immediately falls back to another group, instead of waiting for the timeout. ### What changed - **Proto / state machine**: Add `ALLOCATION_GATED` to `Instance.InstanceStatus` in `instance_manager.proto`. It is a terminal status reachable from `REQUESTED`, mirroring `ALLOCATION_FAILED` (no cloud instance is ever allocated). - **`LaunchNodeError`**: Add a `gated` flag so the provider can signal a scaleGate block rather than a real failure. - **`KubeRayProvider`**: Detect gated worker groups on each sync (`_evaluate_scale_gates`), batch gated in-flight launches per request id, and emit gated `LaunchNodeError`s. Pending pods of gated groups are excluded from the fetched instances so they are not counted as launching/allocated. - **Reconciler**: Transition gated launches `REQUESTED -> ALLOCATION_GATED`, treat the status as inactive/terminal in cleanup, and surface it under `failed_instance_requests` in the autoscaling state. - **`CloudResourceMonitor`**: Deprioritize gated node types the same way as allocation timeouts (handler renamed to `allocation_timeout_or_gated`), so the scheduler picks a different group on the next cycle. ## Related issue number <!-- Link the tracking issue here, e.g. "Closes #XXXXX", or "N/A". --> N/A ### Tests - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_instance_util.py` (transition graph + reachable-from for `ALLOCATION_GATED`) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_node_provider.py` (scaleGate detection, gated in-flight launch fast-fail, nil-gate cases) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_priority_selection.py` (`ALLOCATION_GATED` marks node type unavailable) - `python -m pytest python/ray/autoscaler/v2/tests/test_reconciler.py` > Note: these require the proto to be regenerated so `Instance.ALLOCATION_GATED` > is available in `instance_manager_pb2` before running. ## Duplicate-work check Searched open PRs/issues for scaleGate / `ALLOCATION_GATED` / autoscaler v2 Kueue fallback and found no existing PR covering this change.

signal.title: [Data][1/N] add external shuffle runtime library
signal.text: Adds the file-transport runtime for a new external (on-disk) shuffle variant: TCP wire protocol, per-node ShuffleFileServer actor, connection / fetch primitives, and error classification. This PR lands only the runtime library and its testers required by external shuffle tasks. It's not wired into the plan yet and there's no user-visible behavior change. ## description - Reducers open one arrow flight connection per source ShuffleFileServer, authenticate with a per-shuffle token, and fetch data straight to disk. - ShuffleFileServer will be started by map task to serve reducer's file read request. Upon init, ShuffleFileServer will bind file serving function to a random available port. - Fault tolerance is driven by Ray's actor state (ActorDied / ActorUnavailable / ActorUnschedulable). On mid-fetch TCP failure, the reducer compares endpoints: if the manager was restarted (where the endpoint are likely to be different) we retry in place; if the endpoint is unchanged (which is Ray RPC still works but our TCP path doesn't) it's almost always a network-configuration problem (NetworkPolicy, firewall, routing) that retries to the same manager can't fix, so we surface a terminal ShuffleFileServerAnomalyError. ## Additional information The complete implementation of shuffle is in https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64733, including runtime libraries, external shuffle task definition, plan wiring and a user-visible flag. I plan to do three PRs (1 is runtime libraries, 2 is task definition and wiring, and 3 is the user-visible flag) to gradually merge the complete implementation.

signal.title: [autoscaler v2] Fix handling of multiple node types with same request_id
signal.text: ## Description When multiple instances with different `node_types` share the same `request_id` and all fail to launch, only one instance is transitioned to `ALLOCATION_FAILED`. This happens because `launch_errors` is keyed by `request_id` alone (`Dict[str, LaunchNodeError]`), so later failures overwrite earlier ones — leaving some stuck instances that never reach a terminal state. This PR changes the key to a `(request_id, node_type)` tuple so each `(request_id, node_type)` combination is tracked independently. The scope is limited to `reconciler.py` and its tests; no API surface changes. ## Related issues Closes #65223. Fixes https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/65223 ## Additional information **Changes:** - `reconciler.py`: `launch_errors` key type changed from `str` to `Tuple[str, NodeType]` (`(request_id, node_type)`) - `_try_resolve_pending_allocation`: updated to use the new key format - `test_reconciler.py`: added `test_requested_multiple_node_types_same_request_id_to_allocation_failed` (66 lines, covers 2 node types sharing one request_id) **AI assistance:** This PR was developed with AI assistance. Every changed line has been reviewed and the relevant tests have been run locally by the human submitter.

signal.title: [TPU] Add PyTorch TPU environment variable and runtime_env APIs to Slice and Subslice placement groups
signal.text: ## What do these changes do? This PR introduces APIs to generate PyTorch TPU environment variables (`TORCH_TPU_TOPOLOGY` and `TORCH_TPU_SLICEBUILDER_ADDRESSES`) for TPU pod slices and multi-host sub-slices. ### Key Changes * **`ray.util.tpu.get_torchtpu_env_vars`**: Added a standalone helper to compute `TORCH_TPU_TOPOLOGY` and `TORCH_TPU_SLICEBUILDER_ADDRESSES`, handling 3D (`v4`, `v5p`, `v5litepod`, `v6e`) and 4D (`v7x` dual-chiplet) topology string normalization. * **`SlicePlacementGroup` & `SubslicePlacementGroup` APIs**: Added `.get_tpu_env_vars()` and `.get_tpu_runtime_env()` methods. These two methods currently only set PyTorch related vars, but could be extended in the future as necessary. From my testing I did not find it necessary to set any additional libtpu/XLA env vars for Torch or JAX workloads to work. * `SlicePlacementGroup`: Delegates to `get_torchtpu_env_vars()` for full pod slice topologies. * `SubslicePlacementGroup`: Partitions parent slicebuilder endpoints (`TORCH_TPU_SLICEBUILDER_ADDRESSES`) across multi-host sub-slices using worker ID label selectors (`RAY_NODE_TPU_WORKER_ID_KEY`) to map the address to the correct ID, with fallback to a remote task querying bundle index `0` for the env var when unset locally. * Added `get_tpu_cores_per_chip` and `get_tpu_resource_per_chip` helpers in `ray._private.accelerators.tpu` ## Related issue number https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/64055 ## How was this tested? - [x] Unit Tests - [x] Manual tests - process in comments
